thesis: The pages show only the general Hugging Face dataset mechanics and an unrelated repository's export issue; nothing shows this folder's exporter existing, running, or producing rows, and the one prior attempt at this play published nothing, so the honest conclusion is that this is an unrun plan with no evidence of output yet.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Hugging Face's dataset sharing documentation describes creating a dataset repository and uploading dataset files through the Hub UI.
claims.quote: Click on your profile and select New Dataset to create a new dataset repository. Pick a name for your dataset, and choose whether it is a public or private dataset.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Text file extensions are not tracked by Git LFS by default, and text files greater than 10MB will not be committed and uploaded, per the same page.
claims.quote: Text file extensions are not tracked by Git LFS by default, and if they’re greater than 10MB, they will not be committed and uploaded.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A dataset repository's simplest supported structure is README.md alongside train.csv and test.csv, and it loads with two splits.
claims.quote: my_dataset_repository/ ├── README.md ├── train. csv └── test. csv In this simple case, you’ll get a dataset with two splits: train (containing examples from train.csv ) and test (containing examples from test.csv ).

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Splits and subsets can be declared in a YAML configs field at the top of the README.md dataset card.
claims.quote: If you have multiple files and want to define which file goes into which split, you can use the YAML configs field at the top of your README.md.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: A dataset with a supported structure and file format (.txt, .csv, .parquet, .jsonl and others) is loaded automatically with load_dataset() and gets a dataset viewer on the Hub.
claims.quote: A dataset with a supported structure and file format ( .txt , .csv , .parquet , .jsonl , .mp3 , .jpg , .zip etc.) are loaded automatically with load_dataset() , and it’ll have a dataset viewer on its dataset page on the Hub.
